audit_findings.title: The OE numerator may mix parent earnings with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 25.4% of ACM Shanghai was not parent-owned at 2025-12-31, while consolidated working-capital changes were $177.827 million and PP&E/intangible purchases were $57.655 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor combines parent-attributable earnings with potentially 100% of subsidiary depreciation, working-capital, capital-expenditure and investment adjustments, directly depressing OE and every projected operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income attributable to non-controlling interests is attributable to the minority holders of shares of ACM Shanghai stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The record demonstrates a perimeter inconsistency if the stated construction was used: $94.078 million of parent-attributable income is not on the same ownership basis as consolidated cash-flow adjustments. The exact correction remains unresolved because the adjustments are not allocated by legal entity. Their scale is large relative to the negative $122.0 million anchor and is reasonably capable of materially changing the operating valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct every OE year by legal entity, apply ACMR's contemporaneous economic ownership to ACM Shanghai and its subsidiaries, retain 100% of wholly owned operations, and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to credit common shareholders with cash belonging partly to public subsidiary shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,074.32 million bridge credit; the 26.8% non-parent fraction is up to $287.92 million, or $3.81 per diluted ACMR share, before legal-entity mapping
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated cash and short-term investments are added to ACMR equity without allocating the minority claim or determining which balances are restricted, required operationally or unavailable for upstream distribution.
audit_findings.evidence: Under laws and regulations of mainland China, there are restrictions on the Company’s mainland China subsidiaries with respect to transferring certain of their net assets to the Company either in the form of dividends, loans, or advances.
audit_findings.explanation: The full consolidated bridge credit is demonstrated, while the amount economically attributable to NCI or unavailable to ACMR remains unresolved. The computed $287.92 million ownership-scale exposure equals about 49% of the absolute $587 million base equity result, so it is material to the bridge even though any correction would make the already-negative valuation lower.
audit_findings.action: Map the June 30, 2026 cash and investments by legal owner, identify restricted and operational balances, apply the 73.2% ownership where appropriate, reconcile against the $544.969 million NCI balance, and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: A temporary working-capital shock is compounded as a permanent and growing loss
audit_findings.magnitude: $285.1 million of stated gross working-capital uses, a $215.3 million OE reversal, and operating PVs of negative $1,228 million to negative $2,022 million; normalization effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The model anchors on negative $122.0 million OE and grows that loss indefinitely, causing higher assumed growth to reduce value and embedding the 2025 working-capital absorption in both explicit cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Significant changes in operating asset and liability accounts during the year-ended December 31, 2025 included the following uses of cash: an increase in inve ntories of $108.2 million (note 5), an increase in accounts receivable of $116.1 million (note 4), and a decrease in customer advances of $60.8 million (note 3).
audit_findings.explanation: The incoherent scenario ordering is demonstrated: BULL is worth less than BASE and BEAR solely because positive growth compounds a negative anchor. Inventories, receivables and customer advances produced $285.1 million of gross uses while the company remained profitable. The recurring maintenance portion is unresolved, but the treatment is plainly capable of changing the valuation conclusion because it drives the entire negative operating PV.
audit_findings.action: Separate maintenance working capital from growth and timing investment using historical turnover, customer-acceptance and collection data; model an explicit recovery path and rerun all scenarios, or terminate at the too-hard conclusion without publishing the negative-anchor DCF.

audit_findings.title: The post-year-end ACM Shanghai share sale contradicts the null perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: ownership decreased from 74.6% to 73.2% by 2026-06-30; $110.2 million gross and $86.0 million net proceeds, equal to $1.14 per diluted ACMR share
audit_findings.mechanism: Lower ownership reduces ACMR's future share of subsidiary OE, while the sale proceeds increase parent cash and therefore the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 6, 2026, ACM Shanghai notified the Shanghai Stock Exchange that ACM Research sold 4,801,648 shares of ACM Shanghai at a price of RMB 160.00 (approximately $ 23.05 ) per share.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter change is demonstrated, but its scale does not threaten the present conclusion. The ownership reduction is 1.4 percentage points, or 1.9% of ACMR's former 74.6% interest, and the $86.0 million net proceeds equal only $1.14 per diluted share versus the $82.21 gap between the negative $7.77 base value and the $74.44 market price. The latest-quarter consolidated cash bridge should already contain the proceeds, although exact once-only inclusion must be reconciled.
audit_findings.action: Set the projected ACM Shanghai ownership to 73.2%, trace the $86.0 million net proceeds into June 2026 parent cash, confirm no separate duplicate bridge addition, and rerun the perimeter reconciliation.

audit_findings.title: Subsidiary-level options dilute the numerator without entering the ACMR share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.929 million FY2025 diluted-numerator reduction, equal to 1.6% of the $122.0 million OE anchor; 2,431,900 subsidiary options exercised in May 2026 reduced ownership from 73.6% to 73.2%
audit_findings.mechanism: ACM Shanghai awards reduce ACMR's economic share of subsidiary OE without issuing ACMR shares, so their effect belongs in the parent-attributable OE numerator or ownership percentage rather than ACMR's share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: In the future, ACM Shanghai may issue options, restricted shares and other forms of share-based compensation to its directors, officers and employees, which could dilute ACM Research’s ownership in ACM Shanghai.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim-level dilution is demonstrated, but the filed scale is not material to the current conclusion. The FY2025 diluted-EPS adjustment was $1.929 million versus a $122.0 million anchor, and the 2026 exercises reduced ownership by only 0.4 percentage point. These amounts are small relative to the $82.21 per-share gap between base value and market price, although future grants could accumulate and should be monitored through the ownership calculation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile all exercised and in-the-money ACM Shanghai awards to the 73.2% June ownership, incorporate remaining awards in a subsidiary fully diluted ownership schedule, and verify parent-attributable OE against the ACMR-only denominator.
